stem:
Ira checks whether $2500$ and $8000$ could be perfect cubes by using last-digit and trailing-zero patterns.

Which two claims correctly apply those patterns?

options.text: Call the full answer the label units digit, and stop there.
$8000$ may be a perfect cube: trailing zeros in a cube come in groups of three.
$2500$ cannot be a perfect cube: a cube cannot end in exactly two zeros.
Call $2500$ a cube only because the printed $25$ looks largest on the page.

teacher.key_rationale: Trailing zeros of a perfect cube come in threes, so 8000 is possible and 2500 is not. Naming units digit alone, or grabbing printed 25, miss the trailing-zero test.
